correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge3\), every four-vertex simplex is exactly a pair of disjoint edges by bipartite Konig matching, and five vertices always contain an independent triple. The oriented square boundary 2-form omega_i satisfies delta omega_i=0; the exterior product omega_i wedge omega_j therefore has delta zero and only allowable tetrahedron support. The four vertices of two distinct horizontal edges, one top in square i and one bottom in square j (i<j), have a unique perfect matching. Thus their coefficients form a signed identity N-by-N matrix for the N proposed cycles. The published grid homotopy theorem gives \(H_3\) a free abelian rank N, so projection along the identity minor is a surjective isomorphism over \(\mathbb Z\). Row and column flips reverse both square orientations and hence permute products without signs; counting fixed square-pairs gives the full integral module and coinvariants. The standalone script reconstructs graph and simplices and checks 165 cycles and complete \(\mathbb F_2\) top nullities for n=3..11. The finite checks are not substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: A natural square-pair geometric basis and exact integral action resolve lattice-level ambiguity left by a sphere-wedge classification and rational character calculations. The all-parameter unit coefficient minor is a structural primitive-cycle theorem, not a finite table increment: it determines integrally trivial row swap, exact reflection-orbit decomposition, and torsion-free integer coinvariants. Rational character information alone allows an integral regular module and a split trivial-plus-sign module with different coinvariants; the new result distinguishes them.
